newsitem.title: USA: Canada's Martin sees no room for tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin sees no room for tax cut.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Friday that he will not support a tax cut if government programs could be compromised.

"Nobody wants to bring a tax cut in more than I do, but we will not do it if there is any possiblility that the funding for healthcare, education and old age pensions is in jeopardy," he said in a speech hosted by the Canadian Society of New York.
When asked if tax cuts were considered during the last budget process, Martin said there was a "reasonable amount" of discussion, but they "very quickly rejected the possibility".
"A tax cut at this point in the deficit fight...would simply have been irresponsible," Martin said.
Martin was supportive of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and said it should be extended.
"We would like to see it extended substantially into Latin America. We think it has been a great success."
He was adamently opposed to the creation of legislation which forces nations to balance their budgets.
"I really don't buy it. I have never seen balanced budget legislation that would, in fact, work," he said.
He voiced confidence regarding Quebec's improving economy and said inflation "remains under firm control".
"Setting Quebec aside for a minute, I think there are no risks that anything is going to turn the course we are on -- I just don't think there is anything that will derail it."
He also said: "In terms of economic growth, no other G7 country will do as well as Canada in '97."
